summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Anthropic is the frontier lab that buys compute across three silicon suppliers and, since mid-2026, signs the leases and the generation orders itself — up to 5 GW of Amazon Trainium under a commitment of 'more than $100 billion over the next ten years', 'well over a gigawatt' of Google TPUs in 2026 and 'multiple gigawatts' more from 2027 (recapped by Anthropic as 5 GW), USD 30 billion of Azure and up to 1 GW of NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin, a USD 50 billion Fluidstack data-centre programme, all of SpaceX's Colossus 1 (more than 300 MW), a direct 20-year, 401 MW lease with TeraWulf at Hawesville, Kentucky (about USD 19 billion), a 470 MW equipment purchase order with ERock, and reported six-year contracts of about USD 45 billion with Nscale (460 MW) and USD 35 billion with Lambda — financed by run-rate revenue the company reported at USD 47 billion in May 2026 (USD 9 billion at end-2025), a Series H of USD 65 billion at a USD 965 billion post-money valuation, and a confidential draft S-1 filed on 1 June 2026.

BACKGROUND. A Delaware public benefit corporation founded in 2021 by Dario and Daniela Amodei and five other former OpenAI researchers, governed by a Long-Term Benefit Trust whose appointees have held a board majority since April 2026. Amazon is 'primary cloud provider and training partner' with USD 8 billion of convertible notes (2023–2025) converted in part to preferred stock plus USD 10 billion of Series G and H preferred bought in Q2 2026 and a USD 20 billion milestone facility; Google holds about 14% (court records, per Fortune) after commitments Google has not itself itemised; Microsoft committed up to USD 5 billion and NVIDIA up to USD 10 billion in November 2025. The company sells the Claude model family (Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 from 1 September 2026, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5) through its API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry, Claude Code (USD 2.5 billion run-rate by February 2026) and vertical offerings for finance, life sciences, healthcare and government. It endorsed California SB 53, welcomed New York's RAISE Act, signed the EU GPAI code of practice, argues publicly for chip export controls, pledged to pay '100% of the grid upgrades needed to interconnect our data centers', and won a First Amendment ruling on 28 August 2026 against the Department of War's supply-chain-risk designation. It has not published a consolidated gigawatt total, its headcount, or a fiscal-year revenue figure.
ecosystemRole: The compute buyer this corpus's landlords, utilities and power vendors are building for: named in Amazon's, Google's, Microsoft's and NVIDIA's own releases as the counterparty for gigawatt-denominated silicon; the end user behind Fluidstack's Google-backstopped leases at TeraWulf, Cipher and Hut 8; the direct tenant at TeraWulf's Justified campus and, per Bloomberg, at Riot's Rockdale; ERock's largest-ever order (470 MW of gas gensets); the reported anchor at Nscale's Monarch campus and, through Lambda and NVIDIA, at Hut 8's Beacon Point; and the anchor tenant of Theseus, the Macquarie–GIC platform that will 'develop, own, operate, and lease' facilities to it. Its make-versus-lease answer is neither: it leases buildings, has chips bought by an Apollo–Blackstone vehicle with Broadcom residual-value support, and buys the generation.

productsAndServices.name: Compute procurement — the three-silicon supply book (Amazon Trainium, Google TPU, NVIDIA on Azure and neoclouds)
productsAndServices.description: The capacity Anthropic contracts to train and serve Claude, denominated by the parties in gigawatts: Amazon Trainium2–4 and Graviton under a ten-year commitment of more than USD 100 billion for up to 5 GW; Google TPUs — up to one million chips and 'well over a gigawatt' in 2026, 'multiple gigawatts' from 2027 supplied through Broadcom; NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin on Azure (USD 30 billion, up to 1 GW) and through CoreWeave, Lambda, Nscale, SpaceX/xAI and Volta.
highlights: Amazon (20 April 2026): 'up to 5 gigawatts (GW) of capacity for training and deploying Claude', 'nearly 1GW total' of Trainium capacity 'by the end of 2026'; 'Anthropic is committing more than $100 billion over the next ten years to AWS technologies'; 'over one million Trainium2 chips' in use; Project Rainier at New Carlisle, Indiana — 'nearly half a million Trainium2 chips' (Amazon), 'roughly one gigawatt of power' across Indiana, Mississippi and Pennsylvania (Semafor, quoting an AWS engineer).

Google (23 October 2025): 'up to one million TPU chips', 'well over a gigawatt of capacity coming online in 2026', 'worth tens of billions of dollars'; (6 April 2026): 'multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity … expected to come online starting in 2027', 'supplied through Broadcom' — Anthropic's own May 2026 recap calls it a '5 GW agreement beginning in 2027'; CFO Krishna Rao: 'our most significant compute commitment to date'.

Microsoft and NVIDIA (18 November 2025): 'Anthropic has committed to purchase $30 billion of Azure compute capacity and to contract additional compute capacity up to one gigawatt' on 'NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems'; 'Claude becomes only frontier model on all three major cloud services'.

SpaceX (6 May 2026): 'an agreement with SpaceX to use all of the compute capacity at their Colossus 1 data center, giving access to more than 300 megawatts of new capacity (over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs) within the month'; SpaceX's S-1 terms per TechCrunch: USD 1.25 billion a month through May 2029, 90-day termination.

Neocloud contracts reported in 2026 (none confirmed by Anthropic): CoreWeave multi-year agreement (April); Volta Infra six-year, USD 10 billion, 121 MW IT at Tydal, Norway (August); Nscale about USD 45 billion / 460 MW at Monarch (August); Lambda six-year, USD 35 billion at Hut 8's Beacon Point (August–September); an AMD partnership of USD 5 billion (press tally). Forkast's count: 'eight compute corridors'; TechXplore: 'at least $135 billion' of commitments in 2026.

Anthropic has never published a consolidated total; MeasuredAI's tracker headline is '15+ GW' and DCD cites 'more than 10GW of servers from cloud providers including a $200 billion agreement with Google' — the USD 200 billion figure has no primary source.
productsAndServices.positioning: OpenAI's compute book is larger and NVIDIA-centred (the corpus's openai dossier records ~30 GW committed); Anthropic's is the only frontier book split across three silicon platforms, which its own releases present as 'a disciplined approach to scaling infrastructure' and which The Register and Dealroom present as circular — Amazon, Google, Microsoft and NVIDIA are all shareholders and suppliers.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not sold; contracted. Cloud commitments (take-or-pay style, with Amazon's USD 20 billion facility released 'as we reach certain delivery milestones of compute capacity'), direct leases (TeraWulf, Riot per Bloomberg), tenant-operator programmes (Fluidstack), chip-leasing SPVs (Apollo–Blackstone, Broadcom residual-value support) and an anchor-tenant platform (Theseus).
targetSegments: Claude training runs (Anthropic projects a single model needs '2GW capacity in 2027 and 5GW in 2028')
Inference for API, Claude Code and enterprise customers
productsAndServices.roadmap: Trainium2 capacity H1 2026 and ~1 GW Trainium by end-2026; Fluidstack sites 'online throughout 2026'; Google/Broadcom TPUs 'starting in 2027'; Justified 2H 2027 → early 2028; Riot Rockdale 96 MW December 2027 → 191 MW June 2028; Monarch late 2027; Volta December 2026 and March 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Sites, leases and power — TeraWulf Justified, Fluidstack's five campuses, Riot Rockdale, Hut 8 River Bend and Beacon Point, ERock generation, Theseus
productsAndServices.description: Where Anthropic itself, rather than a cloud, is the tenant, end user or equipment buyer: a 20-year, 401 MW lease at TeraWulf's Justified campus in Hawesville, Kentucky (about USD 19 billion initial term, up to about USD 33 billion with extensions, 'supported by an investment-grade credit'); the USD 50 billion Fluidstack programme whose leases the landlords file under Fluidstack's name with Google backstops; Riot's 191 MW build-to-suit at Rockdale, Texas (USD 9.1 billion over 20 years; tenant unnamed by Riot, Anthropic per Bloomberg); Hut 8's River Bend (245 MW for Anthropic via Fluidstack, up to 2,295 MW) and Beacon Point (704 MW, NVIDIA lease, Lambda operator, Anthropic buyer per CoinDesk); ERock's 470 MW RockBlock order; and Theseus, the Macquarie Asset Management–GIC platform formed to 'develop, own, operate, and lease' facilities to Anthropic.
highlights: TeraWulf (6 July 2026): 'a 20-year lease agreement with Anthropic at its Justified Data campus in Hawesville, Kentucky … approximately 401 MW of critical IT load … approximately $19 billion of contracted revenue over the initial term', 'up to approximately $33 billion if Anthropic exercises both five-year extension options'; initial capacity 'second half of 2027', full 401 MW 'by early 2028'; Fluidstack is not a party (Hoodline; the 8-K).

Fluidstack (12 November 2025): 'a $50 billion investment in American computing infrastructure, building data centers with Fluidstack in Texas and New York, with more sites to come'; the landlords' filings put Fluidstack's leased critical IT at about 1.4 GW (Lake Mariner 378 MW, Abernathy 168 MW, Barber Lake 207 MW, River Bend 245 MW, New Lebanon 430 MW), all Google-backstopped; Hut 8's release: 'at least 245 megawatts and up to 2,295 MW of AI data center infrastructure for Anthropic, leveraging clusters operated by Fluidstack', with Head of Compute James Bradbury quoted.

ERock (11 August 2026): 'Executed a 470 MW equipment purchase order with Anthropic … extending production commitments into 2028'; backlog 'approximately $1.7 billion'; natural-gas RockBlock generators, no sites named — Anthropic has not announced it.

Riot Platforms (10 August 2026): '191 MW critical IT build-to-suit Tier 3 data center at Riot's Rockdale campus', 20 years to June 2048, '$9.1 billion' (USD 16.1 billion with options), 'initial 96 IT MW expected in December 2027', a USD 573 million Morgan Stanley interim facility and an 'IG-Backstop in Finalization'; tenant 'one of the world's leading frontier AI labs' — Anthropic per Bloomberg.

Theseus (Macquarie, 10 August 2026): MAM funds and GIC 'jointly own the platform and provide majority equity funding for each project', Anthropic as anchor tenant, US focus, no capital figure, capacity or sites disclosed; Anthropic commits to cover consumer electricity-price increases from these sites.

Chips at the Fluidstack sites: press accounts of the Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone vehicle (June–September 2026, about USD 35–36 billion in tranches) describe an SPV that 'will purchase Google's chips and lease them to Anthropic for use at facilities in New York, Texas, Louisiana, and Indiana', with Broadcom 'providing a residual value support agreement'; Bloomberg reported Blackstone weighing a second package.
MLQ (2026): 'more than a dozen preliminary agreements to lease U.S. data centers with a combined capacity exceeding 1 gigawatt' — search-summary only.
productsAndServices.positioning: Among frontier labs Anthropic sits between OpenAI (Stargate's landlord-financed campuses through Oracle, Crusoe and SoftBank) and xAI (self-built Colossus): it contracts directly for buildings and generation but owns neither, and its chips at leased sites are owned by lessors. The corpus's terawulf dossier calls the Justified lease 'graduation day' from middleman tenancy.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct leases with investment-grade credit support (the provider is not named in TeraWulf's filings); end-user agreements behind Fluidstack's Google-backstopped leases; equipment purchase orders (ERock); anchor-tenant platform (Theseus).
targetSegments: Anthropic's own training and inference fleet
productsAndServices.roadmap: Lake Mariner CB-4 2H 2026 and CB-5 early 2027; Barber Lake September 2026; Abernathy Q4 2026; River Bend Q2 2027; Justified 2H 2027; Rockdale December 2027; ERock deliveries into 2028.

productsAndServices.name: Claude model family and platform — Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5; Claude Developer Platform, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry
productsAndServices.category: Frontier models and API (the revenue side)
productsAndServices.description: The models the compute serves, sold per token through Anthropic's API and the three hyperscaler marketplaces: Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 (1 September 2026; USD 10 per million input tokens, USD 50 output; Mythos 'identical to Fable 5.1 but with reduced safeguards for verified professionals'), Claude Opus 5 (24 July 2026; USD 5/25), Claude Sonnet 5 (30 June 2026; USD 2/10) and Claude Haiku 4.5 (USD 1/5).
highlights: Fable 5.1 pricing page: cache reads USD 0.25 per million ('75% reduction from Fable 5'); 'US-only inference: 1.1x pricing multiplier'; available on the API, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Azure Foundry, Claude Code and Claude Enterprise; named customers Jane Street, Cognition, Millennium, MongoDB, Square, Ramp, Canva, Datadog and SpaceX AI.

Fable 5 and Mythos 5 (9 June 2026) were withdrawn 12–30 June 2026 after 'the US government applied export controls to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, requiring restriction of access to foreign nationals' (triggered by a safeguard bypass by Amazon researchers), and restored on 1 July 2026 when the controls were lifted.

Distribution: 'Claude becomes only frontier model on all three major cloud services' (November 2025); 'over 100,000 customers running Claude on Amazon Bedrock' (April 2026); 'over 1,000 business customers each spending $1+ million annually' (April 2026); '8' of the Fortune 10 (February 2026).

Run-rate revenue as Anthropic states it: about USD 1 billion early 2025, over USD 5 billion August 2025, USD 14 billion February 2026, over USD 30 billion April 2026 (from about USD 9 billion at end-2025), 'crossed $47 billion' May 2026; Bloomberg (August 2026, sources): USD 65 billion at end-July.
Consumer and team plans (claude.com/pricing): Free; Pro USD 17 a month annual or USD 20 monthly; Max from USD 100; Team USD 20 or USD 100 per seat; Enterprise seat plus usage.
productsAndServices.positioning: Versus OpenAI's GPT-5.5/5.6 and Google's Gemini as the company itself positions each release (Fable 5.1 against 'GPT-5.6 Sol, Opus 5, and previous Fable 5'); enterprise revenue is 'more than 50% of total' (February 2026).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct API and subscriptions; Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry; GSA schedule and the USD 1 government offer; systems integrators (Accenture, Deloitte, KPMG, PwC).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards rollout 'fall 2026'; Mythos trusted-access expansion; Sonnet 5 on Vertex AI 'coming soon'.

productsAndServices.name: Claude Code, Cowork and the agentic products
productsAndServices.description: Claude Code (launched with Claude 3.7 Sonnet, March 2025) — USD 500 million run-rate by September 2025, USD 1 billion by November 2025 'six months after public launch', 'over $2.5 billion' by February 2026 — plus Claude Cowork inside spreadsheets and documents via MCP, the Bun acquisition (December 2025), and Anthropic Labs (January 2026) under Mike Krieger and Ben Mann.
highlights: Team and Enterprise premium seats with Claude Code, admin controls and a Compliance API (August 2025); PwC rollout of Claude Code and Cowork to '30,000 PwC professionals' (May 2026) — Dario Amodei: 'Insurance underwriting that took 10 weeks now takes 10 days'.

Higher usage limits (May 2026) were funded explicitly by the Colossus 1 capacity: 'Anthropic plans to use this additional compute to directly improve capacity for Claude Pro and Claude Max subscribers' (SpaceX AI page).
productsAndServices.positioning: Claude Code is the product the company cites when it explains why it needs more compute; press accounts of mid-2026 rate limits and outages attributed them 'primarily' to a compute shortage.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Subscriptions (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) and API usage.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Anthropic Labs products; Cowork on all plans (per the Opus 4.8 release).

productsAndServices.name: Vertical and public-sector offerings — Claude for Financial Services, Life Sciences, Healthcare, Government (Claude Gov), Enterprise Frontier Safeguards
productsAndServices.description: Packaged deployments with named partners and channels: Financial Services (July 2025; Bridgewater, Commonwealth Bank, AIG; FactSet, S&P Global, Snowflake), Life Sciences (October 2025; Sanofi, Novo Nordisk, Broad Institute), Healthcare (January 2026; HIPAA-ready), Claude Gov for classified environments on AWS (June 2025), the USD 200 million DoD CDAO prototype agreement (July 2025), Claude for USD 1 a year to all three branches of government (August 2025), and Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (September 2026; Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Citi, Visa, Mastercard).

Cal., 28 August 2026) held the designation 'unlawful retaliation' — 'The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics'; the D.C. Circuit case is pending.
DOE Genesis Mission partnership (December 2025) with all 17 national labs, including 'speeding up permitting review processes that bottleneck America's energy expansion'.
Anthropic Economic Index reports (January, March, June 2026) and Claude Corps (USD 150 million, 1,000 fellows, June 2026).
productsAndServices.positioning: The government line is where policy exposure and revenue meet: the company claimed the designation could cut 2026 revenue by 'multiple billions'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: AWS, Google Cloud and Palantir for government; marketplaces; GSA schedule.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards fall 2026; D.C. Circuit ruling pending.

recentDevelopments.headline: Press reports the Broadcom–Apollo–Blackstone chip-leasing platform: an initial tranche of about USD 35 billion to buy Google TPUs and lease them to Anthropic at Fluidstack-based sites in New York, Texas, Louisiana and Indiana from mid-2026, with Broadcom supporting residual value
recentDevelopments.read: The chips are neither the lab's nor the operator's — a lessor vehicle with the chip designer standing behind the residual.

recentDevelopments.headline: Fortune: court documents confirm Google holds 'roughly 14% of Anthropic in straight equity, hard-capped contractually at 15%'; Amazon's percentage 'is not disclosed', estimated 'mid-to-high teens'
recentDevelopments.read: The two strategic stakes that the IPO will have to describe, one public and one not.

recentDevelopments.headline: Confidential draft registration statement on Form S-1 submitted to the SEC for a proposed initial public offering; 'the number of shares to be offered and the price have not yet been set'
recentDevelopments.read: The compute book becomes a disclosure obligation.

recentDevelopments.headline: Series H: USD 65 billion at a USD 965 billion post-money valuation led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia; 'Run-Rate Revenue: Crossed $47 billion'; Micron, Samsung and SK hynix as 'Strategic Infrastructure Partners'; proceeds for research, 'expanded compute capacity' and products
recentDevelopments.read: Memory makers as strategic investors — the supply chain for HBM joins the cap table alongside the cloud suppliers.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'Higher usage limits for Claude and a compute deal with SpaceX': all of Colossus 1's capacity — 'more than 300 megawatts of new capacity (over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs) within the month'; the same post recaps Amazon's 'up to 5 GW', Google/Broadcom's '5 GW agreement beginning in 2027', Microsoft/NVIDIA and Fluidstack
recentDevelopments.read: The only place Anthropic has ever listed its compute book in one paragraph; SpaceX's S-1 later put the price at USD 1.25 billion a month with 90-day termination.

recentDevelopments.headline: CNBC and Bloomberg: Google commits up to USD 40 billion — USD 10 billion now at a USD 350 billion valuation and USD 30 billion on performance milestones — alongside five gigawatts of Google Cloud compute over five years; no Google primary statement located
recentDevelopments.read: Investor and supplier in one commitment, mirroring Amazon's five days earlier.

recentDevelopments.headline: Amazon: 'up to 5 gigawatts (GW) of capacity' for training and deploying Claude, 'more than $100 billion over the next ten years to AWS technologies' spanning Graviton and Trainium2 through Trainium4; Amazon invests USD 5 billion 'today' and 'up to an additional $20 billion' tied to milestones; 'over one million Trainium2 chips' in use
recentDevelopments.read: The largest single supply commitment in the book, to a chip the company co-develops — and the milestone facility ties the investor's cash to the supplier's deliveries.

recentDevelopments.headline: The Long-Term Benefit Trust appoints Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan to the board — 'The appointment expands the Trust's representation to a majority of board seats'
recentDevelopments.read: The governance milestone the 2023 Trust design promised 'within 4 years', delivered before the IPO filing.

recentDevelopments.headline: CoreWeave and Anthropic sign a multi-year compute agreement (value undisclosed; capacity 'later that year' at 'production scale' per DCD); CoreWeave announced Jane Street's USD 6 billion deal five days later
recentDevelopments.read: A fourth NVIDIA-based channel beside Azure, Colossus and Lambda; Anthropic's newsroom is silent.

recentDevelopments.headline: Google and Broadcom: 'multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity expected to come online starting in 2027', 'the vast majority' sited in the United States; CFO Krishna Rao: 'We are making our most significant compute commitment to date'; run-rate revenue 'surpassed $30 billion'
recentDevelopments.read: TPUs bought through the chip designer rather than only the cloud — the supply relationship moves one layer down.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'Where things stand with the Department of War': Anthropic received a supply-chain-risk designation on 4 March 2026, calls it not 'legally sound', will 'challenge it in court', and will provide models to the department 'at nominal cost' during transition; it had refused to permit 'fully autonomous weapons and mass domestic surveillance'
recentDevelopments.read: The company's use restrictions become a federal procurement dispute.

recentDevelopments.headline: Responsible Scaling Policy v3.0 (v3.1 on 2 April 2026): company-only mitigations separated from industry recommendations, a 'Frontier Safety Roadmap' of 'nonbinding but publicly-declared targets', and 'Risk Reports' every three to six months with third-party review in some cases
recentDevelopments.read: The safety framework the SB 53 and RAISE Act regimes now require of large frontier developers.

recentDevelopments.headline: Series G: USD 30 billion at USD 380 billion post-money led by GIC and Coatue with D. E. Shaw, Dragoneer, Founders Fund, ICONIQ and MGX; run-rate revenue USD 14 billion; USD 1 million-plus customers 'from 12 to 500+ in two years'; Claude Code 'over $2.5 billion'
recentDevelopments.read: The round that folded the Microsoft and NVIDIA commitments into a priced financing.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'Covering electricity price increases from our data centers': 'We will pay for 100% of the grid upgrades needed to interconnect our data centers, paid through increases to our monthly electricity charges'; commits to bring new generation online matching its needs; 'US AI sector will need at least 50 gigawatts of capacity over the next several years'
recentDevelopments.read: A buyer's pledge that turns the large-load-tariff argument the corpus's utilities are having into a voluntary commitment — no sites or utilities named.

recentDevelopments.headline: Anthropic Labs formed under Mike Krieger and Ben Mann; Ami Vora takes over Product; Cuéllar joins the LTBT the following week as Kanika Bahl and Zachary Robinson conclude their terms
recentDevelopments.read: Product leadership reshuffled as the company moves from one flagship to a portfolio of agents.

recentDevelopments.headline: SB 53 compliance: 'On January 1, California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act (SB 53) will go into effect'; Anthropic publishes its Frontier Compliance Framework covering cyber, CBRN, sabotage and loss-of-control risks, referencing New York's RAISE Act and the EU AI Act codes as parallel regimes
recentDevelopments.read: The company complies with the state law it endorsed three months before it applies.

recentDevelopments.headline: DOE Genesis Mission partnership with all 17 national laboratories, including 'speeding up permitting review processes that bottleneck America's energy expansion'; a nuclear-risk classifier co-developed with NNSA
recentDevelopments.read: The lab as a permitting-acceleration vendor to the department whose loans and sites it argues should go to AI.

recentDevelopments.headline: Hut 8 announces an AI infrastructure partnership with Anthropic and Fluidstack: 'at least 245 megawatts and up to 2,295 MW' for Anthropic at River Bend, Louisiana and beyond, 'leveraging clusters operated by Fluidstack'; James Bradbury, Head of Compute: 'a new opportunity to collaborate with Hut 8 to bring additional capacity online by early 2027'
recentDevelopments.read: The first landlord release to name Anthropic as the end user behind a Fluidstack lease.

recentDevelopments.headline: Microsoft, NVIDIA and Anthropic: 'Anthropic has committed to purchase $30 billion of Azure compute capacity and to contract additional compute capacity up to one gigawatt' on Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin; NVIDIA 'up to $10 billion' and Microsoft 'up to $5 billion' of investment; 'Amazon remains Anthropic's primary cloud provider and training partner'
recentDevelopments.read: Demand denominated in gigawatts on a third cloud; The Register called it a '$45 billion back-scratching session'.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'Anthropic invests $50 billion in American AI infrastructure' — data centres with Fluidstack in Texas and New York 'with more sites to come', about 800 permanent and 2,400 construction jobs, sites online 'throughout 2026', in support of 'the Trump administration's AI Action Plan'
recentDevelopments.read: The programme behind roughly 1.4 GW of Google-backstopped leases the landlords file under Fluidstack's name.

recentDevelopments.headline: Project Rainier opens at New Carlisle, Indiana: about USD 11 billion, 1,200 acres, seven buildings 'packed wall-to-wall' with Trainium2 — about 500,000 chips with 'a million by the end of the year', 'devoted to a single customer, Anthropic'; Semafor: Rainier spans Indiana, Mississippi and Pennsylvania at roughly one gigawatt
recentDevelopments.read: The largest non-NVIDIA deployment anywhere, built by the investor for the investee.

recentDevelopments.headline: Google Cloud: 'up to one million TPUs', 'well over a gigawatt of capacity coming online in 2026', an expansion 'worth tens of billions of dollars'; Anthropic 'trains and serves on three chip platforms'
recentDevelopments.read: The first gigawatt-denominated commitment in Anthropic's book and the moment TPUs became a merchant product.

recentDevelopments.headline: Rahul Patil (ex-Stripe CTO; AWS, Microsoft, Oracle Cloud) becomes CTO with 'oversight of engineering across product, compute, infrastructure, inference, data science, and security'; Sam McCandlish becomes Chief Architect
recentDevelopments.read: Infrastructure leadership hired from the clouds the company buys from.

recentDevelopments.headline: Anthropic endorses California SB 53 — 'While we believe that frontier AI safety is best addressed at the federal level instead of a patchwork of state regulations, powerful AI advancements won't wait for consensus in Washington'; the bill was signed 29 September 2025
recentDevelopments.read: The first frontier lab to back a state safety statute, three months before the White House ordered a task force against state AI laws.

recentDevelopments.headline: Series F: USD 13 billion at USD 183 billion post-money led by ICONIQ with Fidelity and Lightspeed; run-rate from '~$1 billion' at the start of 2025 to 'over $5 billion' in August; Claude Code '>$500 million'
recentDevelopments.read: The round that preceded, and priced, the autumn compute commitments.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'Build AI in America': the US AI sector 'needs at least 50GW of electric capacity by 2028'; a single model will need '2GW capacity in 2027 and 5GW in 2028'; recommendations on federal lands, NEPA, transmission corridors, geothermal, gas and nuclear permitting; the same day Anthropic says it 'intends to sign' the EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
recentDevelopments.read: The buyer's policy programme: permit the power, and the compute follows.

recentDevelopments.headline: DoD Chief Digital and AI Office awards a two-year prototype other-transaction agreement with a USD 200 million ceiling; Claude Gov models run on AWS infrastructure
recentDevelopments.read: The contract the March 2026 designation put at risk.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'Securing America's Compute Advantage': Anthropic supports the AI Diffusion Rule's tiering with adjustments, a lower no-licence threshold for Tier 2 and more BIS enforcement funding, arguing Chinese firms need '2-4x more power to achieve similar results'
recentDevelopments.read: A compute buyer arguing for scarcity abroad — the export-control posture that later applied to its own model.

recentDevelopments.headline: Series E: USD 3.5 billion at USD 61.5 billion post-money led by Lightspeed; Claude Code launched with Claude 3.7 Sonnet
recentDevelopments.read: The valuation was to rise fifteenfold in fifteen months.

relationships.scale: up to 5 GW; >USD 100 billion over ten years; Amazon USD 8bn notes + USD 10bn preferred + USD 20bn facility
relationships.via: AWS Trainium2/3/4, Graviton; Project Rainier; Amazon Bedrock
relationships.note: Amazon is 'primary cloud provider and training partner' — up to 5 GW of Trainium and Graviton capacity under a commitment of 'more than $100 billion over the next ten years' — and Anthropic's largest investor, with USD 8 billion of convertible notes (2023–2025), USD 10 billion of Series G and H preferred (Q2 2026) and a USD 20 billion facility released on compute-delivery milestones.
relationships.context:
Anthropic (20 April 2026): 'up to 5 gigawatts (GW) of capacity for training and deploying Claude', 'nearly 1GW total' by end-2026, 'over one million Trainium2 chips' in use; Amazon's release: '$5 billion in Anthropic today and up to an additional $20 billion in the future tied to certain commercial milestones'. Amazon's Q2 2026 10-Q: 'From Q3 2023 to Q4 2025, we invested $8.0 billion in convertible notes from Anthropic', partly converted to nonvoting preferred in Q1 2025 and Q1 2026; USD 5.0 billion of Series G and USD 5.0 billion of Series H preferred in Q2 2026; 'an aggregate facility not to exceed $20.0 billion' released 'as we reach certain delivery milestones of compute capacity'; carrying value about USD 190 billion after 'upward adjustments of approximately $50.5 billion in Q2 2026'.

Project Rainier — New Carlisle, Indiana, 'nearly half a million Trainium2 chips', 'devoted to a single customer, Anthropic' (CNBC), spanning Indiana, Mississippi and Pennsylvania at 'roughly one gigawatt' (Semafor) — is the physical anchor; Claude runs on Bedrock for 'over 100,000 customers'. The UK CMA found the partnership did not qualify for investigation (September 2024); the FTC's 6(b) report (January 2025) recorded 'significant equity and certain revenue-sharing rights' across the cloud–lab partnerships. Amazon researchers' safeguard bypass triggered the June 2026 export-control episode on Fable 5.

relationships.scale: up to 1 million TPUs, 'well over a gigawatt' 2026; 'multiple gigawatts' from 2027 (Anthropic recap: 5 GW); ~14% equity
relationships.via: Google Cloud TPUs (Ironwood and next-generation, supplied through Broadcom); Vertex AI
relationships.note: Google supplies TPUs — 'up to one million' with 'well over a gigawatt' in 2026 and 'multiple gigawatts' from 2027 through Broadcom — holds about 14% of Anthropic (court records per Fortune, capped at 15%), backstops Fluidstack's leases at the Anthropic sites, and is Vertex AI's Claude distributor; press reports an up-to-USD 40 billion 2026 commitment that Google has not itself itemised.
relationships.context:
Google Cloud (23 October 2025): 'Anthropic will have access to up to one million TPU chips', 'well over a gigawatt of capacity coming online in 2026', 'worth tens of billions of dollars'; (6 April 2026): 'multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity' 'expected to come online starting in 2027', 'Google-built TPUs supplied through Broadcom'. Anthropic's May 2026 recap: 'Google and Broadcom: 5 GW agreement beginning in 2027'. CNBC and Bloomberg (24 April 2026): USD 10 billion now at a USD 350 billion valuation plus USD 30 billion on milestones and five gigawatts over five years — no Google primary statement was located and Alphabet's Q1 2026 10-Q does not name Anthropic.

The CMA cleared Google's 2023–24 investment ('up to $2 billion') in November 2024. Fortune (June 2026): 'roughly 14% of Anthropic in straight equity, hard-capped contractually at 15%'. Google is also the guarantor of record on every Fluidstack lease serving Anthropic (TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8, Meridian Arc filings) and, per press accounts, the designer of the chips the Apollo–Blackstone vehicle leases to Anthropic. Google pays SpaceX/xAI for Colossus capacity in parallel — the same landlord serves both labs.

relationships.scale: USD 30 billion of Azure; up to 1 GW; Microsoft up to USD 5 billion invested (USD 3.2 billion gain booked July 2026)
relationships.via: Azure (NVIDIA Grace Blackwell / Vera Rubin); Microsoft Foundry; Copilot
relationships.note: Anthropic committed to buy USD 30 billion of Azure capacity and up to 1 GW of NVIDIA systems on Azure (November 2025); Microsoft committed up to USD 5 billion of investment and distributes Claude through Foundry and the Copilot family — and is itself a customer reported at USD 500 million a year.
relationships.context: Microsoft's blog (18 November 2025): 'Anthropic has committed to purchase $30 billion of Azure compute capacity and to contract additional compute capacity up to one gigawatt'; 'NVIDIA and Microsoft are committing to invest up to $10 billion and up to $5 billion respectively'; Claude Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.1 and Haiku 4.5 in Foundry; 'Claude becomes only frontier model on all three major cloud services'. TechCrunch (29 July 2026): Microsoft 'recorded its investment in Anthropic as a $3.2 billion gain' on the USD 5 billion. The Information (via Sherwood, January 2026): Microsoft 'on pace to spend $500 million per year' on Anthropic models for GitHub Copilot and 365 Copilot. In West Virginia the two were counterparties for the same Monarch capacity — Microsoft's LOI, then Anthropic's reported contract.

relationships.scale: up to 1 GW of Grace Blackwell / Vera Rubin on Azure; NVIDIA up to USD 10 billion investment; Colossus 1 '>220,000 NVIDIA GPUs'; lease-holder at Beacon Point (Lambda deal)
relationships.via: Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems on Azure; Colossus 1; Lambda/Hut 8 Beacon Point
relationships.note: NVIDIA committed up to USD 10 billion of investment and 'a deep technology partnership' (November 2025) alongside up to 1 GW of Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity on Azure; NVIDIA GPUs are the silicon at Colossus 1 and, per CoinDesk, NVIDIA holds the Hut 8 Beacon Point lease that Lambda operates for Anthropic; Jensen Huang said in March 2026 the Anthropic investment 'probably will be the last' of its kind.
relationships.context: The November 2025 release: 'For the first time, NVIDIA and Anthropic are establishing a deep technology partnership' to 'optimize Anthropic models for performance, efficiency, and cost, as well as optimizing future NVIDIA architectures for Anthropic workloads'. The corpus's nvidia dossier reads the same deal as demand 'denominated in gigawatts, not units'. In 2026 NVIDIA's role widened: the Colossus 1 agreement gives Anthropic 'over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs'; Dealroom describes NVIDIA 'supplying silicon, providing equity backing to Lambda, and serving as lease anchor' on the USD 35 billion Lambda deal, with NVIDIA's CFO acknowledging the circular-financing charge. NVIDIA's 10-Q line item for the Anthropic investment was not found; BofA's Vivek Arya notes both labs 'are designing their own custom chips'.

relationships.scale: 401 MW critical IT, 20 years, ~USD 19 billion (up to ~USD 33 billion); plus ~546 MW at Lake Mariner and Abernathy via Fluidstack
relationships.via: Justified Data Campus, Hawesville KY (direct lease); Lake Mariner and Abernathy (through Fluidstack)
relationships.note: TeraWulf is Anthropic's landlord twice over: directly at the Justified campus in Hawesville, Kentucky (20 years, about 401 MW, about USD 19 billion initial term, 'supported by an investment-grade credit', July 2026) and indirectly at Lake Mariner (378 MW) and Abernathy (168 MW), where Fluidstack is the tenant behind Google's backstops.
relationships.context:
TeraWulf's 6 July 2026 release: 'The Company has executed a 20-year lease agreement with Anthropic at its Justified Data campus … approximately 401 MW of critical IT load … approximately $19 billion of contracted revenue over the initial term', 'up to approximately $33 billion if Anthropic exercises both five-year extension options'; initial capacity 'second half of 2027', full 401 MW 'by early 2028'; CEO Paul Prager: 'The Anthropic lease validates our strategy'. Fluidstack is not a party (the 8-K; Hoodline). Data Center Frontier's July 2026 analysis flags long-lead electrical equipment — transformers, switchgear, chillers — as the choke point on the schedule.

The Lake Mariner and Abernathy leases never name Anthropic ('a global hyperscale AI platform developing frontier-scale foundation models'); trade press mapped them to the USD 50 billion programme in November 2025 and MeasuredAI reports Anthropic's first TPU capacity live at Lake Mariner on 5 July 2026.

relationships.scale: 470 MW equipment purchase order; ERock backlog ~USD 1.7 billion
relationships.note: ERock (Enchanted Rock) disclosed on 11 August 2026 that it 'executed a 470 MW equipment purchase order with Anthropic', its largest ever, taking its power-system sales backlog to about USD 1.7 billion and 'extending production commitments into 2028'; no sites or delivery dates are named and Anthropic has not announced it.
relationships.context: CEO John Carrington in the Q2 2026 release: 'We secured a 470 MW equipment purchase order from Anthropic, increasing our Contracted Power System Sales Backlog to approximately $1.7 billion and extending our production commitments into 2028.' Hart Energy (via ERock's newsroom) describes natural-gas RockBlock generators with 'lower emissions, quieter operation and no water requirements' bought for 'speed to power'; the corpus's enchanted-rock dossier notes sell-side now frames ERock as 'a play on the Anthropic IPO' and infers Fluidstack's Texas and New York builds as the host — an inference, not a disclosure. The order is an equipment sale plus operations, not a power-purchase agreement: Anthropic will own generation.

relationships.scale: USD 50 billion programme; ~1.4 GW of Google-backstopped leases at TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8 and Meridian Arc
relationships.via: custom-built data centres in Texas, New York, Louisiana and Indiana
relationships.note: Fluidstack is the tenant-operator of Anthropic's USD 50 billion US data-centre programme announced on 12 November 2025 — the leases sit in Fluidstack subsidiaries with Google backstops, the buildings belong to TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8 and Meridian Arc, and the chips are bought by an Apollo–Blackstone vehicle and leased to Anthropic.
relationships.context: Anthropic's release: 'building data centers with Fluidstack in Texas and New York, with more sites to come', chosen 'for its ability to move with exceptional agility, enabling rapid delivery of gigawatts of power'; 'approximately 800 permanent jobs and 2,400 construction jobs'. Hut 8's 17 December 2025 release names Anthropic as end user of the Fluidstack-operated River Bend clusters ('at least 245 megawatts and up to 2,295 MW'). MeasuredAI's reading: 'Anthropic is not a party to the lease and guarantees nothing'. Anthropic's July 2026 Justified lease and its reported Nscale, Lambda and Riot contracts show it now also contracts around Fluidstack.

relationships.scale: >300 MW / >220,000 NVIDIA GPUs (all of Colossus 1); USD 1.25 billion a month through May 2029 per SpaceX's S-1
relationships.note: Anthropic contracted all of Colossus 1's capacity — 'more than 300 megawatts of new capacity (over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs) within the month' — from SpaceX (which now houses xAI) in May 2026; SpaceX's S-1 puts the price at USD 1.25 billion a month through May 2029 with 90-day termination rights.
relationships.context: Anthropic frames the counterparty as SpaceX: 'signed an agreement with SpaceX to use all of the compute capacity at their Colossus 1 data center'; xAI's page: 'SpaceXAI has signed an agreement with Anthropic to provide access to Colossus 1', to 'directly improve capacity for Claude Pro and Claude Max subscribers'. TechCrunch (20 May 2026), from the S-1: USD 1.25 billion per month, 'either party can terminate with 90 days' notice', more than USD 40 billion potential, discounted rates for the first two months. The corpus's xai dossier calls it the most important commercial event in xAI's history — Colossus becomes a merchant cloud — and notes the same announcement floated Anthropic's interest in 'multiple gigawatts' of orbital compute. Google signed for Colossus capacity a month later; the Musk complex is landlord to two rival labs.

relationships.note: CoreWeave and Anthropic signed a multi-year compute agreement in April 2026 (value undisclosed; capacity at 'production scale' later in 2026 per DCD); the corpus's coreweave dossier records it five days before CoreWeave's USD 6 billion Jane Street deal as evidence of diversification beyond Microsoft.
relationships.context: Reported by DCD and Forbes; CoreWeave's own release was not retrieved and Anthropic's newsroom does not mention it. It adds a fourth NVIDIA-based channel (with Azure, Colossus and Lambda) to a book otherwise weighted to Trainium and TPUs.

relationships.scale: reported ~USD 45 billion over six years for ~460 MW at Monarch (unconfirmed by either party)
relationships.via: Vera Rubin capacity at the Monarch Compute Campus, Mason County WV, from late 2027
relationships.note: Press reports (Bloomberg, CNBC, TechCrunch, 26 August 2026) a six-year contract of about USD 45 billion for about 460 MW of Vera Rubin capacity at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia, taking the tranche Microsoft's 1.35 GW letter of intent had covered; Nscale's regulatory disclosure via Aker confirmed a contract without naming the customer.
relationships.context: Semafor: Microsoft 'withdrew from Monarch negotiations over the summer' and Google's talks 'fell through'; West Virginia's governor: 'the reported $45 billion agreement'. Global Data Center Hub's arithmetic — about USD 16.3 million per MW-year, roughly 1.9x an estimated USD 24 billion build — reads the price as delivery certainty. Monarch's power is 2 GW of Caterpillar gas gensets on a state-certified microgrid; capacity is due from late 2027. Neither company has confirmed the name; the corpus's nscale dossier carries the same 'announced' status.

relationships.scale: reported six-year, USD 35 billion; ~350 MW at Hut 8 Beacon Point (NVIDIA lease)
relationships.via: Lambda-operated NVIDIA capacity at Hut 8 Beacon Point, Nueces County TX
relationships.note: Bloomberg (31 August 2026) reported a six-year, USD 35 billion cloud deal with NVIDIA-backed Lambda; CoinDesk and Cryptopolitan place the capacity at Hut 8's Beacon Point in Texas, where NVIDIA secured the lease in July 2026 and Lambda installs the chips — 'Nvidia holding the lease, Lambda handling chip installation, and Anthropic functioning as the end buyer'.
relationships.context: Hut 8 disclosed 'two 15-year leases at Beacon Point covering 704 megawatts of IT capacity without naming the tenant'; NVIDIA's CFO, per Dealroom: 'We recognize the scale of this support, and we know some will call this circular financing. We see it differently.' TechXplore's tally: Anthropic's 2026 compute commitments total 'at least $135 billion'. Neither Lambda's nor Anthropic's release was retrieved.

relationships.scale: 330 MW of utility capacity at River Bend (Hut 8) for 245 MW critical IT serving Anthropic
relationships.via: Entergy Louisiana (River Bend); Entergy Mississippi (AWS, per tracker)
relationships.note: Entergy Louisiana supplies 330 MW of utility capacity to Hut 8's River Bend campus, whose 245 MW Fluidstack lease serves Anthropic per Hut 8's partnership release; Hut 8's project page lists Entergy, Fluidstack and Anthropic as partners.
relationships.context: Entergy's 17 December 2025 release names Fluidstack as tenant 'with financial backing from Google' and Hut 8 as the party paying for generators and substation; the Anthropic link is stated by Hut 8, not Entergy. MeasuredAI's tracker also attributes AWS's Mississippi campus (a Rainier site per Semafor) to Entergy Mississippi — an independent tracker's attribution, not a filing.

relationships.via: frontier models; shared clouds (AWS, Azure, Oracle), shared landlords (Hut 8, SpaceX/xAI, Nscale)
relationships.note: Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers and competes with OpenAI across models, enterprise and the same compute suppliers — AWS sells to both, Microsoft distributes both, Nscale's Stargate sites were OpenAI's before Microsoft's and Anthropic's.
relationships.context: The corpus's openai dossier records OpenAI's USD 38 billion, seven-year AWS agreement and about 30 GW of committed capacity against Anthropic's three-silicon book; the two are the demand behind the 'nearly half' of about USD 2 trillion of cloud backlog CNBC attributes to their commitments. Anthropic's Series H valuation (USD 965 billion) eclipsed OpenAI's per Bloomberg. No commercial relationship exists between the two companies.

relationships.scale: co-lead, USD 30bn Series G; significant investor, USD 65bn Series H
relationships.note: Abu Dhabi's MGX co-led the USD 30 billion Series G (February 2026) and is listed as a significant investor in the USD 65 billion Series H (May 2026); MGX's board calls the Series G a follow-on, so an earlier position existed.
relationships.context: Anthropic's Series G release: 'The round was co-led by D. E. Shaw Ventures, Dragoneer, Founders Fund, ICONIQ, and MGX'; the Series H release lists MGX under 'Significant investors'. Amounts undisclosed. The relationship carries a documented internal debate at Anthropic over Gulf capital (WIRED-reported Amodei memo: 'a real downside and I'm not thrilled about it'; deals to be 'narrowly scoped, purely financial'). MGX's dossier (this corpus) types the reverse link `other` because the schema's `type` enum has no 'portfolio' value.

policyExposure.regime: US export controls — AI Diffusion Rule, H20/H200 China licensing, and the June 2026 controls on Claude Fable 5 / Mythos 5
policyExposure.exposure: Anthropic is a public advocate of chip export controls (April 2025 Diffusion Rule position; July 2025 opposition to the H20 reversal; July 2026 open-weights post calling for anti-smuggling action) and, in June 2026, their object: 'the US government applied export controls to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, requiring restriction of access to foreign nationals' from 12 to 30 June 2026 before the controls were lifted. Commerce's January 2026 rule allowed H200 exports to China under a 25% tariff and volume cap; the Diffusion Rule's rescission is contested (GAO, May 2026).
policyExposure.mitigation: Company statements: 'Anthropic stands by its recently filed public submission'; 'US-only inference' pricing tier (1.1x) on Opus 4.6 and Fable 5.1; September 2025 bar on China-controlled entities.

policyExposure.regime: California SB 53 — Transparency in Frontier AI Act
policyExposure.exposure: Anthropic endorsed SB 53 on 8 September 2025 (the first large lab to do so), the bill was signed 29 September 2025, and the company published its Frontier Compliance Framework on 19 December 2025 covering cyber, CBRN, sabotage and loss-of-control risks; as a frontier developer it must publish a framework and transparency reports and report critical incidents.
policyExposure.mitigation: Responsible Scaling Policy v3.0/v3.1 (February–April 2026) and the Frontier Compliance Framework (company documents).

policyExposure.exposure: Signed 19 December 2025, amended 27 March 2026, effective 1 January 2027: applies to frontier models above 10^26 FLOP and 'large frontier developers' above USD 500 million of revenue, requiring a frontier AI framework, transparency reports and 72-hour critical-incident reporting to NY DFS, with attorney-general penalties up to USD 1 million and USD 3 million. Anthropic's head of external affairs Sarah Heck welcomed it: 'The fact that two of the largest states in the country have now enacted AI transparency legislation … should inspire Congress to build on them.' Anthropic's December 2025 compliance post lists RAISE as a compliance target.
policyExposure.mitigation: The Frontier Compliance Framework published for SB 53 is designed to serve RAISE as well (company statement).

policyExposure.regime: Federal preemption — Executive Order of 11 December 2025 on state AI laws (DOJ AI Litigation Task Force)
policyExposure.exposure: The order directs a DOJ task force to challenge state AI laws, Commerce to list 'onerous' state laws and the FTC to issue a policy statement, with BEAD funding as leverage; Skadden expects a suit against RAISE or SB 53 'is likely'. Anthropic's June 2026 Advanced AI Framework argues Congress 'should not preempt state law unless it enacts a rigorous federal regime that meets or exceeds the strongest measures proposed in the framework'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Public advocacy for 'a single national standard' with a floor (July 2025 AI Action Plan comments; June 2026 framework).

policyExposure.regime: EU AI Act — General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
policyExposure.exposure: Anthropic announced on 21 July 2025 that it 'intends to sign' the Code and appears on the European Commission's list of 21 signatories (updated 31 July 2026) with Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Mistral and OpenAI; the Act's GPAI obligations entered full enforcement on 2 August 2026. The August 2026 Claude text watermark was announced as an EU AI Act compliance measure.

financials.commentary: Anthropic publishes run-rate revenue at funding events and nothing else: no fiscal-year revenue, no gross margin, no compute spend, no burn, no headcount. Every capacity and dollar figure above is either an Anthropic release, a counterparty's filing or release (Amazon's 10-Q is the most detailed), or a named-outlet report marked as such. The Bloomberg USD 65 billion run-rate and every neocloud contract value except Colossus 1's S-1 terms rest on unnamed sources.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Anthropic's compute strategy is a deliberate three-silicon hedge whose price is dependence on suppliers that are also its shareholders. Basis: Trainium (up to 5 GW, more than USD 100 billion over ten years, Amazon holding about USD 190 billion of Anthropic paper), TPUs (well over 1 GW in 2026, multiple GW from 2027, Google about 14%), and NVIDIA on Azure, Colossus, CoreWeave and Lambda (Microsoft up to USD 5 billion, NVIDIA up to USD 10 billion); the company's own phrase is 'a disciplined approach to scaling infrastructure'. Amazon's USD 20 billion facility released 'as we reach certain delivery milestones of compute capacity' makes the investor's cash contingent on the supplier's deliveries — the circularity is contractual, not rhetorical.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that in 2026 Anthropic crossed from cloud customer to direct infrastructure counterparty without becoming an owner. Basis: the 401 MW Justified lease in its own name, Riot's 191 MW build-to-suit (tenant per Bloomberg), the 470 MW ERock equipment order, the Theseus anchor-tenant platform and the Apollo–Blackstone chip vehicle — leases, generation and lessor-owned chips, but no owned campus. This is the make-versus-lease answer the corpus's xai dossier poses: rent the building, buy the power, let a lessor hold the silicon and a hyperscaler hold the credit.

3. **(High confidence)** We assess that power, not chips, is the buyer's binding constraint and that Anthropic is paying to remove it. Basis: 'Build AI in America' (50 GW by 2028; 2 GW per training run in 2027, 5 GW in 2028); the February 2026 pledge to pay '100% of the grid upgrades'; the 470 MW on-site gas order; Monarch's islanded 2 GW; Data Center Frontier's flag that transformers, switchgear and chillers are the choke point on the Justified schedule. The buyer is absorbing costs — grid upgrades, generation, consumer price effects — that utilities' large-load tariffs are only beginning to require.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that delivery-date risk is now larger than allocation risk, and that the 2H 2026 to early 2028 window will show whether the book is real. Basis: Trainium 'nearly 1GW' by end-2026, Fluidstack sites 'throughout 2026' (CB-5 already moved to early 2027), Barber Lake September 2026, River Bend Q2 2027, Justified 2H 2027, Rockdale December 2027, Monarch late 2027, TPUs 'starting in 2027'. No filing read reports a missed milestone yet; the mid-2026 rate limits the company attributed to a compute shortage show what a slip costs. Startup counterparties — Volta was seven months old, Nscale two years — carry the execution.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the run-rate the compute is priced on is real but the numbers after May 2026 are not the company's. Basis: USD 14 billion, USD 30 billion and USD 47 billion are Anthropic statements at funding events; USD 65 billion (Bloomberg, August) and the USD 100–120 billion year-end expectation (FT) are sourced to 'people familiar'. TechXplore's 'at least $135 billion' of 2026 commitments is likewise a press tally. The S-1 will replace all of it; until then the ratio of commitments to revenue is an estimate built on estimates.

6. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that governance and policy posture are assets in the compute market as much as constraints. Basis: LTBT-appointed directors hold a board majority (April 2026) with a former Fed chair as trustee; the company endorsed SB 53, welcomed RAISE, signed the EU code and argues for export controls — and landlords cite 'investment-grade credit' support behind its leases that the filings do not name. The Department of War designation shows the other edge: a policy stance cost a federal customer, and the 28 August ruling recovers it only in one court.

7. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the reported Nscale and Lambda contracts, if confirmed, mark a shift from tenant-of-record intermediaries (Fluidstack behind Google) to neocloud service contracts where the operator finances the build against Anthropic's signature — and that this is what 'investment-grade credit' behind a private company's leases implies. Basis: Nscale's investment-grade-rated term loans and Riot's 'IG-Backstop in Finalization' language; the identity of the credit provider is not disclosed anywhere read, so the mechanism is inferred.

Collection gaps: Anthropic publishes no consolidated capacity total, fiscal-year revenue, compute spend, burn or headcount; the credit-support provider behind the Justified and Rockdale leases is unnamed; Google's own statement of the USD 40 billion commitment, CoreWeave's and Lambda's releases, Nscale's confirmation, the TeraWulf Q2 2026 10-Q text, NVIDIA's 10-Q line item and Amazon's Q1 2026 earnings 8-K were not retrieved; the Jay Kreps board discrepancy is unexplained; several CNBC, DCD, Bloomberg and Forbes pages were unreachable and are cited from search summaries.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — *Q4 2026 — the public S-1:* would replace every press-sourced revenue and commitment figure and name the lease credit support. *End-2026 — 'nearly 1GW' of Trainium and the Fluidstack sites 'online throughout 2026':* the first hard delivery tests of Judgment 4. *Late 2027 — Justified, Rockdale, Monarch and Google/Broadcom TPU first capacity:* the concentration of the book's start dates in one window is itself the risk. *Any ERock site disclosure:* would show where the 470 MW of generation goes and whether it is bridge or permanent power. *D.C. Circuit ruling on the supply-chain-risk designation:* decides whether the federal customer returns. *A confirmed Nscale or Lambda release:* would convert Judgment 7 from inference to record.
